summary.headline: Dhanuka Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9.91% to INR657.51 crore, but management reiterated only a low-single-digit full-year growth and ~100 bps gross margin loss.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 9.9% YoY to INR657.51 crore, with EBITDA of INR152.97 crore and PAT of INR109.22 crore, both up YoY. Growth was driven by insecticides (47% of revenue), which management attributed to El Niño-led product focus and channel agility rather than market share gains. Management said Q2 growth is not a run-rate: it expects low single-digit revenue growth for the full year, with Q3 and Q4 subdued and gross margin down about 100 bps. Analysts probed channel inventory, margin drivers, Dahej plant ramp-up and the new-product index, and management was specific on most points but declined product-level revenue figures.

segments.name: Zones (share of Q2 turnover)
segments.commentary: North 31%, East 12%, West 28%, South 29%. Analyst noted North grew about 22% in Q2 and about 12% in H1; management attributed North strength to irrigated markets.

segments.name: Product categories (share of Q2 revenue)
segments.commentary: Insecticides 47%, fungicides 25%, herbicides 8%, others 20%. Herbicides were hit by dry weather; insecticides grew strongly.

segments.name: Dahej (Harsh Dhanuka)
segments.commentary: Plant at about 70% utilisation per analyst; H1 sales about INR55 crore and H1 EBITDA loss about INR1.79 crore. Two new fungicide products planned in the existing plant, taking the portfolio from 2 to 4 products in FY28; capex amount not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth now guided at low single digit (management clarified this after earlier single-digit guidance; a Q2 growth of about 10% is not a run-rate for Q3 and Q4).
Gross margin expected to fall about 100 bps for the year, with EBITDA decline similar or slightly larger; management said margin expansion will not happen this year.
Q3 and Q4 described as subdued; management does not expect a high sales season in Q3.
Rabi season initial movement described as promising in certain regions; South and East zones are the key for Rabi.
Management said the GST refund effect on gross margin recurs every quarter; excluding it, gross margin is flat.
Biostimulant Dhanzyme Gold liquid formulation approved, launch planned for December 2026.
Dahej capacity expansion approved; new fungicides to be added in FY28. Capex quantum to be clarified in a later round.
Two plant growth regulator and growth influencer launches planned in Q3.
capex_capacity: Dahej plant at about 70% utilisation; capacity expansion of existing products approved along with 2 new fungicide products in the existing plant (FY28).
Capex quantum not disclosed; management said clarity will come in a later round but the company is 'absolutely committed' to capex.
Two R&D centres with NABL-accredited labs; partnerships with 10 multinational agrochemical innovators from Japan, Europe and the US.
Distribution footprint: over 10 million farmers reached via 6,500 distributors, 80,000-plus retailers and 40-plus warehouses.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth attributed to insecticides (LaNevo, Miyako, Mortar, Decis), plant growth regulators and nutritional products; management said this was product-specific, not market share gain.
Chilli in South and cotton (repeat insecticide sprays) and vegetables in East supported demand; fungicide demand was weak.

Generic crop pricing under severe pressure; management said tepid demand prevents full pass-through of raw material cost increases. Some raw materials fell in Q2 and others rose; increases passed on selectively.

Channel inventory described as optimal; company said it cleans channel monthly and did not front-load in Q1. Analyst asked about receivables jump; management said debtors are not aggressively placed and material is taken back quickly.

Farmer purchasing power constrained: commodity prices high but rainfall-dependent farmers reduced, per management; fertiliser e-Token and enforcement cited as reducing fertiliser-linked tagging of crop protection sales.
Polin (paddy fungicide from Nippon Soda, Japan) priced above market acceptance; not expected to scale near term.
Brazil and European subsidiaries are for registration only; customers appointed in about 14 countries, purchase orders in hand from 5.

qa_highlights.question: What drove about 10% growth in Q2 and was there regional share gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was product-specific insecticide growth from El Niño-driven re-planning, plus focus on water-available areas and no Q1 channel front-loading. Q2 growth is not an indicator for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10% growth a run-rate, and will growth moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained single-digit growth guidance for the year, saying Q2 growth reflects the weak base of last year's same quarter and is not indicative of Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong North performance (about 22% in Q2) market share gain or industry-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said North irrigated markets (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) were industry's favourite; it would not confirm share gain.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin held despite lowest ITI and high-margin mix moderation: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross margin was slightly lower YoY due to GST refund effects; EBITDA margin improved mainly from tighter other expenses. Value growth (10%) exceeded volume growth (6%).

qa_highlights.question: Full-year guidance: high single digit or double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Dhanuka said the company will grow by a single low digit for the year, with gross margin down about 100 bps and EBITDA down similarly or slightly more.

qa_highlights.question: Will product-level revenue such as LaNevo be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product-specific revenue, though it said LaNevo was a leading growth driver in Q2.

risks_watch: Full-year guidance cut to low single-digit growth; Q3 and Q4 subdued, with weak demand in the Western and Central regions where rain opportunity has ended.
Gross margin pressure of about 100 bps; competitors' high-cost inventory could pressure generic pricing in H2.
Dahej remains loss-making; capex quantum and timelines for the two new fungicides not yet disclosed.
Enforcement against unregistered and spurious products; industry-wide concern flagged, with FICCI involvement.
Rabi season performance in South and East zones is the key swing factor.
New-product index (ITI) moderation; Polin unlikely to scale near term, pipeline depends on Q3 PGR launches and Dhanzyme Gold December launch.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q2 execution and insecticide-led resilience, but cautious and explicit about H2: management repeatedly tempered the Q2 print and lowered full-year expectations. Evasive on product-level revenues and capex amounts.
key_quotes: This indeed is a product-specific growth from the domain of insecticides.
So this 10% growth is not an indication of what we can expect in other two quarters.
So about 100 bps less in gross margin.
I think so the position is that we'll be growing by a single low digit, and that is where we are.
